summary: The root cause of INC-002 is cfg-2207, the infra-automation cost-optimisation profile applied to portfolio-service at 2026-03-10T09:52:00Z, which cut db.pool.max_size from 50 to 5 and exhausted the JDBC connection pool on the portfolio holdings path (confidence 0.80, high; top hypothesis clearly ahead of the rejected alternatives). At 60s resolution both api-gateway and portfolio-service were flat-healthy through the 09:52Z minute and stepped together in the 09:53Z minute, so onset is strictly after the cap change; portfolio-service then logged HikariPool-1 exhaustion (total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=43) and JDBC acquire timeouts, causing 503s upstream and gateway 504 'upstream timeout portfolio-service' on /v1/portfolio/holdings. Traffic (526-596 req/s) and portfolio-service CPU/memory were flat, so the new cap — not load or resource starvation — is the binding constraint. The reporter's suspicion, the 08:00Z gateway HTTP/2 upgrade dep-5220, is undermined: it precedes onset by 108 minutes with no intermediate drift, shows a timeout-not-reset signature, and cannot produce an upstream JDBC-acquire error.

ranked_hypotheses.title: cfg-2207 shrank the portfolio-service JDBC pool 50→5, exhausting connections and stalling the portfolio path
ranked_hypotheses.statement: At 09:52Z infra-automation applied cost-optimisation profile 'small' to portfolio-service's datasource, cutting db.pool.max_size from 50 to 5 (cfg-2207). The cap took effect at ~09:52-09:54Z (db_pool_in_use locks at exactly 5.0 from 09:54Z). Concurrent holdings queries then had to share 5 connections; the waiting queue reached 43 and requests failed to acquire a JDBC connection within 3000ms. portfolio-service fell over to 503s and its p99 jumped from ~173ms to ~4.25s in the same 09:53Z minute. The gateway, routing /v1/portfolio/* to portfolio-service, blocked on that upstream and returned 504 'upstream timeout portfolio-service' from 09:53:53Z. Both the gateway and upstream latency/error steps now resolve to the 09:53-09:54Z minute, i.e. strictly AFTER cfg-2207 applied at 09:52Z, and both series were flat-healthy through 09:52Z inclusive.

causal_chain.claim: cfg-2207 applied at 09:52Z sets portfolio-service db.pool.max_size 50 -> 5
Pool cap takes effect: db_pool_in_use falls and then locks at exactly 5.0 from 09:54Z, matching the new cap
No load step accompanied the onset: request_rate flat 526-596 req/s across 09:30-10:10Z
Concurrent holdings queries exceed 5 connections; HikariPool-1 exhaustion: total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=43; 'could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms'
portfolio-service latency steps from 172.69ms (09:52Z) to 4250.91ms in the 09:53Z minute and error rate steps from 0.25% to 22.3% at 09:54Z

api-gateway, blocked on the slow upstream, emits 504 'upstream timeout portfolio-service GET /v1/portfolio/holdings' from 09:53:53Z, and its p99 steps in the same 09:53Z minute (gateway does not lead the upstream)

Sentinel: all four shared-dependency co-tenants (order-service, payment-service on ledger-db; auth-service, market-data-service on redis-cache) stay flat in latency and error rate, and market-data-service - a direct portfolio-service downstream - stays at 38-41ms while its caller stalls

assumptions: The service's concurrency/connection demand at ~09:52Z exceeded 5 (43 waiters observed post-change supports this, but the pre-change waiting depth was never measured; db_pool_in_use was only ~11.5-12.7 of the old 50, consistent with a modest but real demand above 5).

The true onset instant is the 09:53Z minute. This is now supported by 60s-resolution data (F19/F20/F23) and supersedes the coarser 09:45-09:50Z and 09:48Z readings in F7/F11, which are 5-minute/irregular buckets that aggregate across the step.
The DB behind the pool was healthy at onset. Indirect support: ledger-db cpu_pct flat ~28.7-31.0% and no co-tenant degradation; no direct ledger-db latency metric was obtainable.
No untracked change to market-data-service/exchange-gateway/ledger-db/redis-cache at 09:52-09:54Z (change-history coverage incomplete for those components).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Independent degradation of a shared downstream (ledger-db / redis-cache / market-data-service) slowed portfolio-service
ranked_hypotheses.statement: portfolio-service's downstreams ledger-db, market-data-service and redis-cache — and via market-data-service, exchange-gateway — are shared with other services (F4). An independently degraded shared component (e.g. ledger-db, the precedent seen in HIST-102 for the identical symptom) slows portfolio-service's holdings query, so it holds JDBC connections longer than 3000ms, driving pool exhaustion and, transitively, gateway 504s. The gateway upgrade and the pool config are coincidental amplifiers.

causal_chain.claim: A shared downstream (ledger-db / redis-cache / market-data-service / exchange-gateway) degrades independently
portfolio-service holdings queries hold JDBC connections >3000ms, so the pool is drained
Errors surface as 'could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms' and pool exhaustion, timing out at 3s
portfolio-service p99 rises to ~4.1-4.3s; gateway times out upstream -> 504s

assumptions: A shared downstream was degraded at exactly ~09:52-09:53Z without any effect on its other consumers.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Its own discriminating prediction was tested and failed: all four co-tenants of the shared dependencies (order-service and payment-service on ledger-db; auth-service and market-data-service on redis-cache) stayed flat in both latency and error rate through the onset bucket, and market-data-service - a direct portfolio-service downstream - remained at 38-41ms (F24-F29). ledger-db cpu_pct was flat ~28.7-31.0% (F35). The failure is also confined to the portfolio path at the very minute the pool cap changed (F31), which the shared-dependency story does not explain.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Untracked deployment/config change to market-data-service or another portfolio-path dependency
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The change-history query could not cover market-data-service, exchange-gateway, ledger-db or redis-cache (budget_exhausted), so a deployment or config change on one of those components could have coincided with onset and slowed the portfolio path. This would resolve the timing conflict between dep-5220 (too early) and cfg-2207 (too late relative to the 09:45-09:50Z bucket).

causal_chain.claim: An unqueried component on the portfolio path received a deployment or config change around 09:45-09:52Z
That change slows portfolio-service's downstream calls, causing connection holds and pool exhaustion

assumptions: F1/F13/F3 assert count-complete change queries, but only for the 2026-03-09T12:00Z-2026-03-10T10:05Z window and for the services queried; market-data-service/exchange-gateway/ledger-db/redis-cache were never verified.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: The timing conflict that motivated H4 no longer exists: 60s-resolution data shows onset at the 09:53Z minute, immediately after cfg-2207 at 09:52Z (F19, F20, F23). Additionally, market-data-service (the named candidate) shows no degradation at all (F27, F29), so a change there is not needed to explain the stall.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Gateway HTTP/2-to-upstreams upgrade (dep-5220) introduced a connection/stream-handling regression
ranked_hypotheses.statement: dep-5220 (api-gateway v9.3.0, 08:00Z) switched envoy 1.29->1.30 and enabled HTTP/2 to portfolio-service and order-service. The upgraded filter chain mishandles upstream H2 connections/streams, so requests to portfolio-service hang until the upstream timeout, yielding p99~4.4s and 504s on /v1/portfolio/*. This is the reporter's suspicion and mirrors HIST-116.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5220 deployed 08:00Z: envoy 1.29->1.30, upstream protocol h2 for portfolio-service and order-service
New envoy/H2 stream handling limits concurrency or resets streams to portfolio-service
Requests stall until the gateway upstream timeout and the gateway emits 504s on /v1/portfolio/*
Users see the portfolio page spin and time out

assumptions: H2 stream-pool/connection-count regression would produce hangs rather than immediate resets.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Decisively undermined by fine-grained telemetry: (1) gateway latency was flat ~200-210ms through 09:52Z, 108 minutes after the deploy, with no intermediate drift, and the step is the 09:53Z minute (F19, F23); (2) the gateway does not lead the upstream - both step together in the 09:53Z minute (F20); (3) the upstream-only 5xx step (22.3%) dwarfs the gateway's (7.18%), and the upstream's own error is a JDBC connection-acquire timeout, which a gateway H2 regression cannot produce (F21, F10); (4) gateway CPU is flat, and the historical HTTP/2 incident's reset signature is absent (F12, F17). Roughly coincidental in time and wrong in mechanism.

facts.statement: cfg-2207 changed portfolio-service db.pool.max_size from 50 to 5 at 2026-03-10T09:52:00Z, authored by infra-automation, described as 'Apply cost-optimisation profile 'small' to service datasource'; it is the latest change before onset and is not reverted in the data.

No deployment exists for portfolio-service itself in the window, so the portfolio-path service change was configuration-only, matching the pool-misconfiguration precedent HIST-115 rather than a code release.
Only one deployment occurred across all services in the window: dep-5220 on api-gateway v9.3.0 at 2026-03-10T08:00:00Z (envoy 1.29->1.30, HTTP/2 to upstreams), status live, 108 minutes before onset.

At 60s resolution, api-gateway p99 was flat ~200-210ms through the 09:52Z bucket and stepped to 4418.76ms in the 09:53Z bucket; portfolio-service p99 was flat ~172-178ms through 09:52Z and stepped in the same 09:53Z bucket to 4250.91ms — the two step together, and both step after 09:52Z.
The fine-grained data supersedes the coarser 5-minute/irregular buckets that placed onset in 09:45-09:50Z; the 09:52Z bucket in that series aggregates the 09:52 and 09:53 minutes.

portfolio-service db_pool_in_use was low and stable (~11.5-12.7 of the old cap of 50) through 09:50Z, then locked at exactly 5.0 from 09:54Z onward, matching the new db.pool.max_size=5; the cap change took effect at ~09:52-09:54Z.

portfolio-service logged 503 ERROR entries from 09:53:19Z, dominated by 'could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms' (270) and HikariPool-1 exhaustion 'request timed out after 3000ms (total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=43)'.

The gateway error signature is a downstream timeout to portfolio-service: 252 WARN 'upstream timeout portfolio-service GET /v<n>/portfolio/holdings' returning 504, first at 09:53:53Z, with only one 'after connection reset' entry in the same batch.

Error rates stepped after 09:52Z and one minute later than latency: portfolio-service 5xx jumped to 22.3% in the 09:54Z bucket versus the gateway's 7.18%, i.e. the upstream error magnitude dwarfs the gateway's.

portfolio-service request_rate was flat (526.33-595.78 req/s across 09:30-10:10Z, no step at 09:45-09:55Z) and CPU (~34-38%) and memory (~54-61%) were unremarkable, so the stall is neither a load step nor resource starvation.

All four shared-dependency co-tenants stayed flat through the onset bucket: order-service p99 ~146-153ms, payment-service ~310-327ms, auth-service ~90ms, market-data-service ~38-41ms, with flat error rates.
ledger-db cpu_pct was flat ~28.7-31.0% across 09:30-10:09Z, weighing against a shared-datastore slowdown as the trigger.
api-gateway CPU was flat ~40.9-43.7% throughout the p99>4s window and the historical HTTP/2 incident's reset signature is absent, weighing against the gateway H2 regression.
api-gateway routes /v1/portfolio/* to portfolio-service, whose downstreams are ledger-db (shared), market-data-service (http) and redis-cache (shared).

Historical precedents are split: HIST-116 (HTTP/2 gateway upgrade, bad_deployment, resolved by gateway rollback), HIST-115 (datasource pool size overridden by a wrong environment profile, config_change), and HIST-102 (identical symptoms from a ledger-db failure) — precedent alone does not discriminate the cause.

assumptions: Concurrency/connection demand on portfolio-service at ~09:52Z exceeded 5 — supported by the 43 observed waiters and by db_pool_in_use of ~11.5-12.7 under the old cap of 50, but the pre-change waiting depth was never measured.

The true onset instant is the 09:53Z minute, per 60s-resolution data (F19/F20/F23); this supersedes the coarser 09:45-09:50Z and 09:48Z readings, which are 5-minute/irregular buckets aggregating across the step.
The database behind the JDBC pool was healthy at onset — indirect support only (ledger-db cpu_pct flat ~28.7-31.0%, no co-tenant degradation); no direct ledger-db latency metric was obtainable.
No untracked change occurred on market-data-service, exchange-gateway, ledger-db or redis-cache at 09:52-09:54Z (change-history coverage for those components is incomplete).
The gateway emits its 504s at WARN level, so the absence of gateway ERROR-level logs is a level-classification artifact, not evidence of gateway health.

(demoted from facts: no verified observation backs it) market-data-service, a direct portfolio-service downstream, stayed healthy at 38-41ms while its caller portfolio-service stalled at ~4.1-4.3s p99, indicating the stall originates inside portfolio-service's own pool resource rather than at its http/cache dependencies.

timeline.event: dep-5220 deployed to api-gateway (v9.3.0): envoy 1.29->1.30 and HTTP/2 enabled to portfolio-service and order-service. Gateway latency remains flat ~200-210ms for the next 112 minutes, with no intermediate drift.
cfg-2207 applied by infra-automation: portfolio-service db.pool.max_size cut from 50 to 5 ('cost-optimisation profile small').
Both api-gateway and portfolio-service p99 still flat-healthy in the 09:52Z minute (gateway 200.33ms, portfolio-service 172.69ms); db_pool_in_use drops from ~11.98 toward the new cap.
Latency steps in the 09:53Z minute on both sides simultaneously: gateway p99 4418.76ms, portfolio-service p99 4250.91ms.
portfolio-service begins logging 503 errors, dominated by 'could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms' and HikariPool-1 exhaustion (total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=43).
First gateway 504 on GET /v1/portfolio/holdings: 'upstream timeout portfolio-service' (252 such WARN entries follow).
Error rates step: portfolio-service 5xx to 22.3% and gateway 5xx to 7.18%; db_pool_in_use locks at exactly 5.0 from this bucket onward.

ledger-db cpu_pct remains flat (30.76%) and all four shared-dependency co-tenants (order-service, payment-service, auth-service, market-data-service) remain flat in latency and error rate across the onset.
Incident reported by on-call SRE: portfolio page spinning/timeouts, gateway p99 > 4s, 504s on /v1/portfolio/*; reporter suspects the gateway upgrade.
Latest data: gateway p99 sustained ~4.28-4.41s and portfolio-service 5xx sustained ~21.5-23.2%; neither change shows a recorded rollback.

recommended_actions.action: Immediate: revert cfg-2207 — restore portfolio-service db.pool.max_size from 5 back to 50 (via the same infra-automation config path, i.e. roll back the 'small' cost-optimisation profile for this datasource) and confirm the change is applied to the running service instance.
recommended_actions.rationale: The cap of 5 is the binding constraint: db_pool_in_use locked at exactly 5.0 from 09:54Z (F31), the pool logged total=5/active=5/idle=0/waiting=43, and errors are JDBC acquire timeouts (F10) that began ~1 minute after the cap change (F2/F14) while latency stepped in the 09:53Z minute (F19/F20).

recommended_actions.action: Immediate: do NOT roll back the api-gateway dep-5220 deployment as the first mitigation; leave gateway version v9.3.0 in place unless a gateway-specific fault emerges.
recommended_actions.rationale: The gateway upgrade precedes onset by 108 minutes with flat latency throughout (F1/F13/F19/F23), shows a timeout-not-reset signature (F9/F17), and cannot produce an upstream JDBC-acquire error (F10/F21); a rollback would discard the sole remaining rejected-cause check while the actual fix is the pool cap.

recommended_actions.action: Short term: verify recovery — watch portfolio-service db_pool_in_use, latency_p99_ms, error_rate and api-gateway p99/5xx for the first 10 minutes after the revert; de-dupe on db_pool_in_use rising above 5 back toward the ~11.5-12.7 baseline and gateway 'upstream timeout portfolio-service' WARNs stopping. Confirm db_pool_in_use no longer pins at exactly 5.0 and error_rate returns to <0.3%.
recommended_actions.rationale: Baseline values are known from pre-change telemetry (db_pool_in_use ~11.45-11.98 at cap 50, latency ~172-190ms, error rate ~0.11-0.25%), so recovery is measurable (F31, F32, F33).

recommended_actions.action: Short term: pull the missing direct telemetry — first retrieve available_metrics for ledger-db, redis-cache and exchange-gateway, then query their latency/health series for 09:40Z-10:00Z, plus ledger-db slow_queries_per_min and replication_lag_ms, and co-tenant db_pool_in_use for order-service/payment-service.
recommended_actions.rationale: These queries were never executed (budget exhausted), so the 'pool too small' vs 'queries too slow' question rests on indirect evidence; direct shared-store health would confirm the DB was not contributing to connection hold-time (F35, F24-F28).

recommended_actions.action: Short term: confirm change attribution and process — record cfg-2207 as the incident cause in the change record and validate whether other services received the same 'small' cost-optimisation profile with a similarly low pool cap.
recommended_actions.rationale: cfg-2207 is the latest change before onset and the change is config-only, matching the HIST-115 pool-misconfiguration precedent; the same automation could have applied the profile elsewhere (F2, F14, F5, F15, F6).

recommended_actions.action: Long term: add guardrails to the cost-optimisation profile automation — a minimum pool-size floor, a canary/staged rollout with automatic rollback on pool-exhaustion or acquire-timeout signals, and a pre-apply check against observed pool demand.
recommended_actions.rationale: The change cut a cap of 50 to 5 despite observed demand of ~11.5-12.7 connections, a 2x+ oversubscription, and produced a service-wide 22.3% error rate within two minutes (F31, F21, F33).

recommended_actions.action: Long term: instrument pool saturation explicitly — add db_pool_waiters / connection-acquire latency metrics to portfolio-service and alert on sustained waiter depth or acquire timeouts, since the service exposes only db_pool_in_use, which saturates at the cap and cannot show over-subscribed demand.
recommended_actions.rationale: Exhaustion magnitude was visible only via error_rate (22.3%) and the log line 'waiting=43'; db_pool_in_use read exactly 5.0 (the cap) and no waiters/acquire-time metric exists (F31, F10, F21).

data_gaps: Change history is incomplete for market-data-service, exchange-gateway, ledger-db and redis-cache (budget exhausted), so an unnoticed deployment/config change on those components before 2026-03-09T12:00Z or after 2026-03-10T10:05Z cannot be fully excluded.

No direct ledger-db, redis-cache or exchange-gateway latency/health series were retrieved for 09:40Z-10:00Z (budget_exhausted), and it is unknown whether ledger-db exposes latency_p99_ms at all; the absence of shared-dependency degradation rests on flat co-tenant latency/error metrics and ledger-db cpu_pct, not on the datastores' own latency.
ledger-db slow_queries_per_min and replication_lag_ms were not fetched, so a brief query-time spike at onset that increased connection hold-time cannot be fully excluded on metrics alone.

portfolio-service exposes no JDBC acquire-time, query-duration or pool-waiter-depth metric (db_query_duration_ms returned not_found), and db_pool_in_use pins at exactly the cap (5.0), so the pre-change waiting depth and the absolute oversubscription magnitude are inferable only from the post-onset log line 'waiting=43'.

No rollback/revert event data was obtainable (no rollback endpoint in the toolset; dep-5220 shows rolled_back_at null and no revert of cfg-2207 appears in the window), so which change responders later treated as suspect is unknown.
Historical search returned only summary fields for HIST-116/HIST-115/HIST-102, so their symptom signatures cannot be contrasted in the detail needed for a discriminating comparison.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Fine-grained telemetry showing a gateway latency/error step at or before 09:52Z (rather than the observed flat-through-09:52Z, step-in-09:53Z pattern) would restore the dep-5220/H2 timing case.

Evidence that portfolio-service's JDBC pool was already saturated and timing out BEFORE cfg-2207 applied at 09:52Z (pre-change db_pool_in_use at or near 50, or acquire-timeout logs before 09:53Z) would invalidate the causal ordering.
Direct ledger-db/redis-cache/exchange-gateway latency or slow-query degradation at 09:52-09:53Z, with co-tenant impact, would support H3 and displace the pool-cap explanation.
Discovery of a deployment or config change on market-data-service, exchange-gateway, ledger-db or redis-cache coincident with onset (currently unqueryable) would reopen H4.

A gateway error signature of upstream resets / HTTP/2 stream-limit errors rather than the observed downstream timeouts, plus gateway-side resource anomaly at onset, would support the reporter's H2 suspicion.

Demonstration that portfolio-service concurrency demand never exceeded 5 connections (i.e. queries were simply slow enough to hold 5 connections >3000ms even though demand was below the old cap's comfort level) would shift the mechanism from 'cap too small' toward query/hold-time degradation.

findings.statement: Timing correlation alone: the gateway deploy at 08:00Z is 108 min before onset with no recorded intermediate degradation, while cfg-2207 at 09:52Z is ~1 min before the first pool error — the change that precedes onset by a plausible, tightly-coupled margin is cfg-2207, not dep-5220.

At 60-second resolution, api-gateway p99 latency is flat ~200-210ms through the 09:52Z bucket (09:48Z=210.22, 09:49Z=208.74, 09:50Z=201.16, 09:51Z=201.64, 09:52Z=200.33ms) and steps up abruptly in the 09:53Z bucket to 4418.76ms, staying at 4228-4359ms through 09:56Z. The gateway latency step occurs in the minute beginning 09:53:00Z, i.e. AFTER 09:52Z, not at or before it.

portfolio-service p99 latency at 60-second resolution is flat ~172-178ms through the 09:52Z bucket (09:52Z=172.69ms) and steps up in the same 09:53Z bucket to 4250.91ms, then 4546.3/4075.33/4046.3ms through 09:56Z. The upstream-side latency step is in the same minute as the gateway's (09:53Z) -- the gateway does NOT lead the upstream; they step together.

Error rates also step AFTER 09:52Z and one minute later than latency: gateway 5xx is 0.21-0.30% through 09:53Z and jumps to 7.18% in the 09:54Z bucket (7.74% at 09:55Z); portfolio-service 5xx is 0.18-0.26% through 09:53Z and jumps to 22.3% in the 09:54Z bucket. The upstream 5xx step (22.3%) is far larger in magnitude than the gateway's (7.18%), consistent with errors originating at portfolio-service.

Wider 120s buckets over 09:40Z-10:00Z show both series healthy before the step: gateway p99 avg 199-212ms for 09:40-09:50Z then 2309.55ms at 09:52Z and 4293-4493ms from 09:54Z; portfolio-service p99 avg 174-190ms for 09:40-09:50Z then 2211.8ms at 09:52Z and 3863-4438ms from 09:54Z. The 09:52Z bucket aggregates the 09:52 and 09:53 minutes, which the 60s data resolves to the 09:53 minute.

Both series were already flat-healthy across the entire 09:40Z-09:52Z span (well after the 08:00Z gateway deploy dep-5220 and including the 09:52Z cfg-2207 apply minute), so 60s resolution rules out any gateway or portfolio-service latency/error step AT or BEFORE 09:52Z: the earliest step in either series is the 09:53Z minute.

order-service (a ledger-db co-tenant) shows no degradation at the ~09:48Z onset: p99 flat at 146.21ms avg / 149.34ms max in the 09:48Z bucket vs 148-153ms in all adjacent 3-min buckets (09:30Z-10:09Z, min 136.95ms, max 162.83ms), and error rate stayed at 0.21% avg in the 09:48Z bucket (range 0.1-0.32% across the whole 09:30Z-10:10Z window).

payment-service (the other ledger-db co-tenant) also shows no degradation: p99 stayed in a narrow ~310-327ms band, 323.21ms avg / 331.1ms max in the 09:48Z bucket (window min 296.68ms, max 340.3ms), with no step change; error rate stayed at 0.17-0.28% with 0.24% avg in the 09:48Z bucket.

auth-service (a redis-cache co-tenant) shows no degradation: p99 flat ~90ms, 90.19ms avg / 92.41ms max in the 09:48Z bucket, and 89.46-91.98ms in every bucket through 10:09Z; error rate remained 0.16-0.31% (0.23% avg in the 09:48Z bucket, no sustained rise).

market-data-service (the other redis-cache co-tenant and a direct portfolio-service downstream) shows no degradation: p99 stayed ~38-41ms (39.04ms avg / 40.76ms max in the 09:48Z bucket; window max 43.82ms) and error rate stayed ~0.14-0.24% (0.22% avg at 09:48Z) across 09:30Z-10:10Z. The fourth co-tenant in the dependency graph is therefore also unaffected.

Interpretation: all four shared-dependency co-tenants (order-service and payment-service on ledger-db; auth-service and market-data-service on redis-cache) have flat latency and flat error rate through the exact bucket in which portfolio-service and api-gateway jump (portfolio-service p99 182ms -> 1719.66ms avg at 09:48Z per F11; gateway 200-230ms -> 1849.99ms avg at 09:50Z per F7). No co-tenant degrades starting at ~09:48Z, so the H3 signature of simultaneous shared-dependency degradation is absent in these metrics.

The degradation is confined to the portfolio path: market-data-service, which portfolio-service calls directly, was healthy at 38-41ms while its caller portfolio-service stalled at ~4.1-4.3s p99, indicating the stall originates at/inside portfolio-service's own resource rather than at its downstream http/cache dependencies.

portfolio-service request_rate/throughput was flat across the whole 09:30-10:10Z window: every 120s bucket avg ranges 526.33-595.78 req/s, with pre-onset buckets ~545-579 and 09:45-09:55Z buckets at 562.27 (09:46), 567.69 (09:48), 549.5 (09:50), 567.17 (09:52), 556.27 (09:54). No load step occurred at 09:45-09:50Z; traffic was unchanged before and after exhaustion.

portfolio-service db_pool_in_use was low and stable (~11.5-12.7 connections) through 09:50Z, far below the then-active cap of 50: 11.45 (09:48Z), 11.98 (09:50Z). It then dropped to avg 8.45/max 11.89 in the 09:52Z bucket and locked at avg=5.0/max=5.0 from 09:54Z onward — matching the new db.pool.max_size=5, i.e. the cap change took effect at ~09:52-09:54Z. No pre-09:52Z pool saturation is visible in the cap-50 era.

portfolio-service latency_p99_ms was flat ~172-190ms through the 09:50Z bucket (09:46Z avg 174.13, 09:48Z avg 178.08, 09:50Z avg 177.94) and then jumped in the very next bucket: 09:52Z avg 2211.8/max 4250.91, 09:54Z avg 4310.82/max 4546.3. Onset is therefore in the 09:52Z bucket, coincident with the pool cap change, not at 09:45-09:50Z.

portfolio-service error_rate was ~0.11-0.25% flat through the 09:52Z bucket (09:50Z avg 0.21, 09:52Z avg 0.25), then stepped to 22.3% at 09:54Z and sustained ~21.5-23.2% thereafter. Error onset is strictly after the 09:52Z pool change, not before.

portfolio-service resource metrics were unremarkable throughout: cpu_pct flat ~34-38% (09:48Z 35.94, 09:52Z 35.46, 09:54Z 34.76; min 33.99 max 38.52) and memory_pct flat ~54-61% (09:50Z 58.88, 09:54Z 57.38; min 53.55 max 60.89). No CPU or memory saturation accompanies the exhaustion, so the stall is not resource-starvation of the service.

ledger-db (portfolio-service's shared DB downstream) shows no degradation: cpu_pct flat ~28.7-31.0% across 09:30-10:09Z (09:48Z 28.65, 09:54Z 30.76). Its available_metrics are connections_active, cpu_pct, disk_used_pct, replication_lag_ms, slow_queries_per_min — it exposes neither a slow-query nor latency metric that spiked in the fine window. This weighs against H3 (shared downstream slowdown) as the trigger.
